answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by forcing each identity to lock a small pigment of bonded value. This bond generates a continuous plume of attested activity that must bridge successive epochs via unique proofs of consistent computation. Attackers creating many fakes must stake large total capital and sustain an independent plume for every identity%3B any shared hardware pattern or gap breaks the bridge and slashes the pigment%2C making mass forgery far costlier than the rewards it can extract.
